item.title: MAGA-Loving Elon Musk Says He's 'Not MAGA,' Feels 'Foolish' Over Spending $445 Million On Dud Republican Midterm Election Campaigns
item.text:
MAGA-Loving Elon Musk Says He's 'Not MAGA,' Feels 'Foolish' Over Spending $445 Million On Dud Republican Midterm Election Campaigns
Good morning! It's Friday, November 20, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most important stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.
In this morning's edition, Elon Musk knows he blew $500 million on the 2026 midterms, General Motors wants to double the money it makes off the war machine, Japan's largest automakers are banding together to standardize some processes and Mercedes-Benz says some German plants are in jeopardy as work stoppages spread.
If you'd like a recap of the latest auto news sent to your inbox each weekday, you can sign up for Jalopnik's free Morning Shift newsletter here.
1st Gear: Elon knows he set nearly $500 million on fire during the '26 midterm elections
It's no secret that Republicans across the U.S. went through an all-time drubbing during the midterm elections earlier this month, and while there were many losers, perhaps none was as big as Elon Musk. The Tesla CEO and Republican version of George Soros dropped over $445 million during the election cycle in a futile attempt to get his candidates into office. That very much didn't work, and now he has buyers remorse.
In truth, it's possible that the garish sums of money Elon spent on the election may have hurt the candidates he backed more than helped them, providing opponents with easy targets to latch onto. I mean, it's not hard to claim that the guy you're running against is back by Big Money when the world's richest man is bankrolling their campaign.
In any case, Elon really wishes he could turn back time, and he's about to have a hell of a lot more to answer for when it comes to his companies as emboldened Democratic leaders vow to investigate Trump and his buddies. From Bloomberg:
"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," the billionaire said late Wednesday at the New York Times' DealBook Summit. "Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money."
[...]
Musk's political money overwhelmingly went to lost causes. Two super political action committees he funded — America PAC and Texas PAC — spent heavily to back Republican Senate and House candidates who lost, Federal Election Commission filings show. Ken Paxton's unsuccessful bid to win Texas' open Senate seat drew the lion's share of the money, at some $229 million.
Democrats also won major races further down the ballot in Texas, where Musk has built much of his corporate empire. Tesla has a sprawling factory near Austin, SpaceX launches rockets from its coastal hub reincorporated as Starbase, and the two companies plan to jointly build a chip factory called Terafab.
Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has taken issue with departing Governor Greg Abbott agreeing to award $1.7 billion in tax breaks for the Terafab project and singled out other state grants SpaceX has received. She called for an immediate moratorium on data center development during her campaign and accused developers of raising utility rates and depleting water supply.
Musk nevertheless downplayed the likelihood of any conflict with Hinojosa, saying he expects her to be "quite moderate."
"I don't think she's a far-left governor," he said. "Based on everything I've heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas."
[...]
When asked about the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee telling Trump and unspecified corporate actors to lawyer up, Musk said some in the party were being "a little over the top."
[...]
During his appearance over a livestream from China, Musk sought to distance himself from the Make American Great Again movement, describing himself as ideologically moderate. "I'm not MAGA," he said.
Technically, Musk is correct. He's not MAGA. As he told supporters in 2024, he is actually "Dark MAGA."
2nd Gear: GM wants to double what it makes off defense
General Motors wants to expand the money it makes off of wars by more than doubling its defense revenue to $2 billion in the next few years. It looks to take advantage of global defense companies turning to its automotive technology to accelerate their weapons production.
Back in August, GM delivered its first batch of Patriot missile components to Lockheed Martin within 22 days of the two companies entering a partnership in weapons manufacturing — something championed by the Trump administration. Several other large defense companies with governmental ties have also lined up to sign deals with GM. From the Financial Times:
"We have massive manufacturing capabilities to build defence equipment components. We have so many defence companies coming to us and saying help us," Stephen duMont, head of GM Defense, said in an interview in London.
In recent years, companies including Volkswagen, Jaguar Land Rover and Renault have diversified into the defence sector in search of new sources of revenue as profits become squeezed in the traditional automotive business due to cut-throat competition and higher costs.
Jim Farley, Ford's chief executive, confirmed earlier this year that it was also in discussions with the US government on defence-related projects, while Stellantis last week agreed to sell its Brampton plant to Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel and explore "global collaboration".
GM's ties to defence stretch back decades. It played a pivotal part in America's "Arsenal of Democracy" campaign during the second world war, converting all of its US plants to support the war effort. The group sold its defence business in 2003 and later re-established GM Defense as a subsidiary in 2017 after Mary Barra became chief executive.
"Mary recognised from early on the opportunity to leverage GM's investment in the automotive business for profitable growth of the defence business," said duMont, a former Raytheon executive.
The defence unit, a separate subsidiary that now has about 500 to 600 employees, was "like a start-up", allowing for quicker decision-making and operational changes.
In the grand scheme of things (read: General Motors), the defense unit is minuscule. It only generates about $1 billion in revenue every year, which isn't exactly nothing, but when compared with the group's total revenue of $185 billion, it's sort of small potatoes. That's why CEO Mary Barra wants to expand it.
It isn't just parts of weapons, either. It's also vehicles. The U.S. Army recently increased orders for Infantry Squad Vehicles from an initial 649 vehicles to nearly 12,000 — which could lead to a $1 billion contract. In addition, it's looking at getting in on the defense business in Europe and the UK.
The business of war is booming, and GM wants in on the action.
3rd Gear: Japans largest automakers are standardizing components to fight China
Japan's largest automakers, including Toyota, Honda and Nissan, are starting a new initiative to compete less and collaborate more as a way to deal with cheap Chinese competition. The first three things they'll do are harmonize quality criteria for steel, unify recycling protocols for plastics, and create a universal color-coding scheme for wire harnesses, but more steps are on the way. The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association says these and any other big changes are coming to any suppliers doing business with Japanese automakers. From Automotive News:
Discussions will begin with Japanese suppliers but soon encompass international ones.
JAMA Chairman Koji Sato, who is also vice chairman of Toyota Motor Corp., launched the campaign after taking the helm of the industry lobby group in January. Leaders announced an agreement on steel, resin, and wire harnesses at the group's last regular meeting of the year here to set the stage for implementing harmonization from 2027.
The urgent efficiency drive is one of the most ambitious attempts yet to reshape a sprawling supply base spanning Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi and Suzuki. The goal: sharpen Japan Inc.'s edge amid an onslaught of new technologies and cutthroat new competitors from China by cutting costs and channeling the savings into innovation.
"We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change," Sato said. "Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas."
A JAMA task force leading the push has been working all year to formulate a framework. They decided on steel, resin and wire harnesses partly because they are areas of the vehicle that go unnoticed by customers and do not directly impact brand value or differentiation. The areas also account for a large portion of a vehicle's input costs, allowing for a large immediate impact.
JAMA said about 70,000 variants of wire harnesses are a prime candidate for consolidation.

Koenigsegg Is Now Worth $1.4 Billion After New Investment
Christian von Koenigsegg will continue to lead the company’s strategy, innovation, and product vision.
A major financial boost for Koenigsegg has revealed its valuation. The Swedish automaker has secured new investment from a private equity firm, and the deal reportedly values the company at about €1.3 billion ($1.4 billion at today’s exchange rate).
The deal with 65 Equity Partners, a Singapore-based private equity firm that is now a minority shareholder, “will enable Koenigsegg to accelerate its expansion and technology development as well as its business systems,” according to the press release announcing the agreement.
Koenigsegg has grown considerably in recent years, reporting €155 million ($170.4 million) in revenue for 2025. That represents a growth of approximately 80 percent since 2022. Demand continues to outstrip production, with the company employing approximately 800 people worldwide.
Christian Von Koenigsegg
Under the agreement, 65 Equity Partners will invest €20 million in Koenigsegg. It will become a minority shareholder and the company's second institutional investor, according to Bloomberg. Chieftain Capital Management, an existing shareholder, will invest additional money, increasing its ownership stake.
Christian von Koenigsegg, the company's founder and CEO, will remain its majority owner. He will continue to lead the company's strategy, innovation, and product vision. Koenigsegg said of the deal:
‘This partnership gives us additional resources to bring our ambitions to life, while preserving the entrepreneurial spirit and engineering freedom that define Koenigsegg.’
The company’s chief financial officer, Johan Ekdah, told Bloomberg that the deal is “not about raising cash,” adding that the company can fund its own projects. It does create “headroom for the future.”
Koenigsegg Gemera
Koenigsegg has started Gemera production, a four-passenger hypercar first unveiled in 2020. It has 2,300 horsepower and 2,028 pound-feet of torque, and the company plans to produce 300.

This Blacked-Out Bentley Torcal Is Limited To Just 20 Units
Stealth wealth looks best in black
Bentley hasn't even delivered its first Torcal yet, but it's already going on its second limited-edition version of the all-electric SUV. First, there was the aptly named Torcal First Edition, and now the automaker has revealed a new bespoke commission. This blacked-out beast has been crafted by Japanese streetwear designer Hiroshi Fujiwara, and just 20 units will be built. For interested shoppers who are looking for an EV that doesn't shout about being electric, this might be it.
Each will be painted in Beluga black, which pairs well with the black badges, blacked-out grille, and the stunning 22-inch Vortex wheels that, you guessed it, are black. Unlike some EV wheels that have uninspired aero discs designed to improve aerodynamics, these fully forged wheels have carbon fiber inserts that look cool while slicing through the air.
Fujiwara founded Tokyo design label FRGMT in 2003, and this special Torcal features some of the company's branding. Positioned on the front fenders is small Bentley // FRGMT text, and there's also an FRGMT logo on the tailgate.
Just like the exterior, the interior of this Torcal is dark and stealthy, revealing a combination of Imperial Blue and Beluga black trim with cross-stitching and piano black accents. Dozens of small FRGMT and Bentley logos have been added to the SUV's door panels, and there are also unique treadplates for some added Japanese streetwear style.
The Torcal is an all-electric conquerer
Bentley announced that the Torcal is already sold out for the first model year, but it hasn't released much info about this blacked-out special, including which markets will get it, how much it will cost, or if it's based on the standard Torcal or the higher-spec Torcal S. The Bentley Torcal will launch as a 2028 model in the U.S. and start at $222,150, including a hefty $4,150 in destination, title, taxes, and dealer charges.
All versions of the 2028 Bentley Torcal use a 113-kWh battery pack and an 800-volt electrical architecture. The standard model rocks two electric motors with 810 horsepower and 881 pound-feet (1,194 Nm), while the Torcal S lifts these figures to 876 hp and 996 lb-ft (1,350 Nm) during launch control. Despite the EV's size and 2,700 kg (almost 6,000 pounds) curb weight, it needs just 2.8 seconds to hit 60 mph (96 kph), making it quicker than a Porsche 911 GT3 RS off the line.
It's not just the sheer performance on offer that makes the Torcal seem impressive. It supports DC charging speeds of up to 400 kW, meaning the battery can be charged from 10-80% in less than 20 minutes. The quoted driving range of up to 375 miles (600 km) isn't industry-leading, but if you live somewhere with ample fast-charging stations, that shouldn't be a big deal.

item.text:
VW Revives Golf GTI Rabbit Edition In The U.S.
The limited-run hot hatch borrows from the Golf R and Europe’s GTI Edition 50, but skips one key upgrade.
VW has unveiled a special Rabbit Edition for the 2027 Golf GTI in the U.S., reviving a nameplate that was last used in 2019. The limited-edition model comes with several visual and chassis upgrades but has not received any alterations to the engine.
The highlight of the Rabbit Edition is the distinctive Dark Moss Green Metallic paint. It's the same as that found on the Golf GTI Edition 50 sold in Europe. This paint has a beautiful metallic finish with shiny flakes that glisten in the sun, and that's just in these photos. We bet it looks even better in person. The special touches made to the Rabbit Edition don't end with the paint.
It borrows parts from the Golf R Black Edition, like the black VW logos, black grille, and black accents around the headlights. The hot hatch also sits on a set of lovely black 19-inch wheels clad in summer performance tires, has a black roof, and black wing mirrors. The only touch of color on the outside, other than the green paint, is the red brake calipers and the red GTI badges. A small rabbit emblem is positioned on the tailgate. VW has made some minor tweaks to the car's cabin, wrapping the seats in a suede-like material with quilted stitching and red accents.
The engine is the same, but the suspension is better
As mentioned, VW hasn't messed with the car's engine. As such, the familiar turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 EA888 continues to deliver 241 horsepower and 273 pound-feet of torque and is mated to a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission. That's a bit of a shame, as the European GTI Edition 50, from which the Rabbit Edition gets its special paint finish, is significantly more powerful. Its 2.0-liter turbo has been tuned to make 321 hp and 310 lb-ft. If buyers want to make those kinds of figures in America, they'll need to turn to the aftermarket.
There is one key performance change that will help the Rabbit Edition perform better than a base Golf GTI on a track and across a mountain pass. It comes standard with the usually optional DCC adaptive damping system, which reacts to the road and steering inputs to automatically adjust the damping at each corner. These dampers are ordinarily only found on America's Golf GTI Autobahn model.
VW will announce prices for the Golf GTI Rabbit Edition before sales kick off in the second quarter of 2027.

item.title: 2027.5 VW GTI Rabbit Edition Aims for the Goldilocks Spot in the Lineup
item.text:
Mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first. But the latest in that tradition, the 2027.5 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition, doesn’t just split the difference between 2027 and 2028; it also slides between the S and SE models that make up the lower tiers of the lineup, while bringing along some of the sweet features from the top-shelf GTI Autobahn trim. In other words, it has the makings of a Goldilocks special.
First, a dash of history. “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S. and Canadian markets back in the days of the Mk1, including on the first GTI that arrived in 1979 in the Great White North and in ‘83 in the States. (The company then returned to the Rabbit name for the Mk5 Golf here, but that’s less consequential—or memorable.) In honor of that first GTI, this new trim includes an adorable little chrome bunny on its hatch, in addition to blacked-out mirror caps, grille, and other trim bits scattered around the exterior that replace red items on other members of the current GTI family.
The GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record. The 19-inch black wheels come from the Golf R, and are wrapped as standard in summer performance tires, versus the all-season rubber that normally comes with less-expensive GTIs. But the most notable change on the fun side is the presence of the DCC adaptive dampers, for which you otherwise would have to spring for the top-shelf Autobahn trim to get. Inside, meanwhile, the Rabbit Edition picks up the GTI SE’s GTI Clubsport ArtVelours material on its comfy yet supportive front buckets and rear bench.
Like all other current GTIs, unfortunately, the Rabbit Edition forces buyers to use a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic to change the gears tied to its 241-horsepower turbocharged inline-four; the manual gearbox remains locked in the past. Still, if you can look past that, the Rabbit Edition has the makings of a steal. Volkswagen hasn’t announced pricing yet—that’ll come closer to its on-sale date of Q2 2027—but seeing as how the carmaker is quite explicit about where it lands in the lineup, expect it to come in the $36,250 of the GTI S and the $40,240 of the GTI SE, plus or minus any little price bumps they might pick up in the next half model year.

Totem Automobili has taken another run at the Alfa Romeo GTA and it might be just be the most seductive Italian since Sophia Loren.
With a timeless beauty combined with hypercar power the $1.3 M GTAmodificata takes Alfa’s 105-series to a whole new level.
Modelled on the 1970 and 1971 European Touring Car Championship-winning GTAm built by Autodelta, Totem’s car retains its classic look, complete with exposed rivets, although the monocoque and bodywork is actually all carbon fiber. Aluminum is used for the front and rear subframes to keep weight down to a paltry 1095 kg (2414 lbs), while the 3.2-liter twin-turbo V-6 from Italtecnica delivers 810 hp and 538 lbft of torque. For comparison, the Ferrari SF90 makes 786 hp and weighs almost 1500 lbs more.
The 90-degree V-6 features dry sump lubrication, individual throttle bodies and a 3D-printed stainless steel exhaust manifold. Back in 1971 the GTAm Touring Car produced 240 hp and that was no slouch, but with more than three times the horsepower the Totem GTAmodificata can dispatch 62 mph from a standstill in 2.6 seconds and reach a vMax of 186 mph. This prodigious power is sent to the rear wheels via a six-speed sequential transmission and limited-slip differential.
With 200 horsepower more than the company’s previous GT Super and GT Electric, the GTAmodificata is also lighter, eschewing paint (for the most part) in favor of exposed carbon fiber outside and in. Even the stunning dished wheels, which evoke the classic GTA, use lightweight carbon and aluminum to save weight.
The GTAmodificato marks the end of the line for Totem’s Giulia GT-inspired cars and just five will be made.

Totem Automobili has taken another run at the Alfa Romeo GTA and it might be just be the most seductive Italian since Sophia Loren.
With a timeless beauty combined with hypercar power the $1.3 M GTAmodificata takes Alfa’s 105-series to a whole new level.
Modelled on the 1970 and 1971 European Touring Car Championship-winning GTAm built by Autodelta, Totem’s car retains its classic look, complete with exposed rivets, although the monocoque and bodywork is actually all carbon fiber. Aluminum is used for the front and rear subframes to keep weight down to a paltry 1095 kg (2414 lbs), while the 3.2-liter twin-turbo V-6 from Italtecnica delivers 810 hp and 538 lbft of torque. For comparison, the Ferrari SF90 makes 786 hp and weighs almost 1500 lbs more.
The 90-degree V-6 features dry sump lubrication, individual throttle bodies and a 3D-printed stainless steel exhaust manifold. Back in 1971 the GTAm Touring Car produced 240 hp and that was no slouch, but with more than three times the horsepower the Totem GTAmodificata can dispatch 62 mph from a standstill in 2.6 seconds and reach a vMax of 186 mph. This prodigious power is sent to the rear wheels via a six-speed sequential transmission and limited-slip differential.
With 200 horsepower more than the company’s previous GT Super and GT Electric, the GTAmodificata is also lighter, eschewing paint (for the most part) in favor of exposed carbon fiber outside and in. Even the stunning dished wheels, which evoke the classic GTA, use lightweight carbon and aluminum to save weight.
The GTAmodificato marks the end of the line for Totem’s Giulia GT-inspired cars and just five will be made.

item.title: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Reportedly Standardize Vehicle Parts in Bid to Lower Costs
item.angle: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs
item.text:
- Toyota, Nissan, and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News.
- The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses.
- Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon.
Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.
In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.
The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.
The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.
“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”

item.title: 2027 Toyota Sienna Refreshed to Give the Hybrid Minivan More Efficiency and Power
item.angle: 2027 Toyota Sienna Refreshed to Give the Hybrid Minivan More Efficiency and Power
item.text:
- Toyota’s 2027 Sienna mid-cycle refresh focuses on improvements under the skin.
- A new sixth-gen hybrid system both makes more power and offers better fuel economy.
- Arriving at dealers in early 2027, the revised Sienna is estimated to start around $44,500.
Some mid-cycle updates focus on aesthetics, bringing some new style (and hopefully some new eyes) to a slightly older product. The 2027 Toyota Sienna skipped those pleasantries and focused on the meat and potatoes: its hybrid powertrain.
The 2027 Toyota Sienna looks no different—unless you count the Cypress paint color, which was dropped and swapped with Storm Cloud—but it’s what’s lying under the body that matters more here. The Sienna adopts Toyota’s sixth-generation hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the upscale Lexus ES Hybrid. A new electric motor packs more efficient silicon-carbide conductors, and it pairs with a 1.15-kWh battery that ditches the old nickel-metal hydride chemistry in favor of lithium-ion. In addition, there’s a whole new electrical platform underpinning it all, with new ECUs and software to manage everything.
Combine all that with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine that has been retuned for quieter low-speed operation, and you have a Toyota Sienna that produces a whopping six horsepower more than before, rising from 245 horses to 251. Engine torque is unchanged at 176 pound-feet, and Toyota did not specify e-motor torque. That small power bump is enough to affect its acceleration: Toyota estimates a 7.5-second sprint to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive Sienna variants, rising to 7.6 seconds with AWD. That’s 0.3 or 0.4 second quicker than before, respectively.
Even with that bump in speed, Toyota claims improved fuel economy in the 2027 Sienna, to the tune of +3 mpg in the city for FWD models and +4 mpg in the city for AWD models. Combined estimates rise 1 or 2 mpg. For context, the 2026 model is EPA estimated at 36 mpg city/36 highway/36 combined for the front-driver, and 35/36/35 for the AWD.
There have also been some tweaks to other electrical-adjacent components. The electronic power steering promises less effort at low speeds, while improving on-center feel at highway speeds. That adjustment includes a new steering-wheel layout that will eventually migrate to other sixth-gen-equipped hybrids. Toyota also fiddled with its brake electronics, resulting in less pedal effort and a smoother blend between regen and friction braking. The Sienna also includes something Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels with the aim to reduce body roll during cornering.
Creature comforts get some upgrades as well. A 12.3-inch infotainment screen is now standard across the lineup (the LE grade ditches its 8.0-incher), as is a 12.3-inch gauge cluster (LE and XLE get this instead of the old 7.0-inch getup). There’s new LED cabin lighting, plus a revised rear-seat entertainment system that now features native apps on a new touchscreen. Upgraded dashboard sound abatement promises to lower the cabin volume by one decibel.
Toyota also slimmed down the Sienna’s trims for 2027. The Limited grade has been dropped in favor of adding more features to the sporty XSE variant, which rises to become the trim underneath the Platinum. As a result, the 2027 Sienna XSE picks up niceties like ventilated front seats with memory, a panoramic-view monitor, and a head-up display. The rugged Woodland Edition trim also picks up the surround-view tech. The upgraded rear-seat entertainment is available on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum trims.
The 2027 Toyota Sienna reaches dealerships in early—you guessed it—2027. Pricing starts around $44,500 for the front-wheel-drive LE base trim, which represents a price bump of less than $2000 over a base 2026 Sienna. Not too shabby for a whole new generation of powertrain.
